# Breadcrumb

Universal element component for navigation breadcrumbs. / /* `items` defaults to `[]` even though its prop type is `isRequired`. A required prop is a lint, not a guarantee: React renders anyway, and `items.map` on `undefined` took the whole page down rather than the one breadcrumb. Found by `DocumentedContract.stories.jsx`, and only once this component's page gained a Usage tab: the guard renders each DOCUMENTED prop against fabricated required props, and it cannot fabricate an `arrayOf(shape)`. So documenting `separator` is what first rendered a Breadcrumb with no items, and the crash had been reachable by any caller all along.

Also asked as: path, navigation trail.

## Usage

Use `Breadcrumb` when a page sits inside a hierarchy the user needs to see and
climb — a student inside a cohort inside a program, a lesson inside a unit. It
answers two questions at once: where am I, and what is one level up.

It takes a single `items` array, ordered root first. Each item is `{ text, href,
onClick }`. The last item is the current page and is rendered as plain text; every
item before it is a link.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name each level as the page is titled, in sentence case. | Abbreviate or invent a shorter name that appears nowhere else. |
| Keep each name to a few words so the trail fits on one line. | Repeat the full page title when it runs long. |
| End the trail on the current page. | Add a trailing link, arrow or the word “current”. |
| Use real nouns: “Autumn 2026”, “Lessons”. | Use “here”, “back” or “click”. |

## Best practices

### The last item is always the current page, whatever you pass it. {#the-last-item-is-always-the-current-page-whatever-you-pass-it}

```jsx
// Incorrect — the href is dropped. The last item is rendered active
// unconditionally, and an active item is plain text with aria-current="page",
// never an anchor.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', href: '/cohorts' },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026', href: '/cohorts/a26' },
]} />

// Correct — the trail ends at where you are.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', href: '/cohorts' },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026' },
]} />
```

### An item with `onClick` still needs an `href`. {#an-item-with-onclick-still-needs-an-href}

```jsx
// Incorrect — with no href the item is rendered active, which means it is an
// li rather than a link. The click handler still fires for a mouse, and is
// unreachable by keyboard.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', onClick: goToCohorts },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026' },
]} />

// Correct — the href makes it a real, focusable link; onClick intercepts it
// for the router. The component calls preventDefault for you.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', href: '/cohorts', onClick: goToCohorts },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026' },
]} />
```

### `separator` takes a string, not a node. {#separator-takes-a-string-not-a-node}

Despite the `node` prop type, the value is written into Bootstrap's breadcrumb
divider custom property, and a custom property holds text. A string is quoted
for you and works; a React element is stringified by CSS and disappears. Pass
`'/'`, `'›'`, `'—'`.

Do: A string separator is quoted for you.
Don't: A React element is stringified by CSS and disappears.

### Show the whole path, root first. {#show-the-whole-path-root-first}

A trail that starts mid-hierarchy leaves people unsure where they are. List every level from the top down to the current page, and let the row wrap rather than dropping a level.

Do: Every level from the root to the current page.
Don't: The trail starts mid-hierarchy, so the top is missing.

### Use it for position, not for history. {#use-it-for-position-not-for-history}

A breadcrumb shows where a page sits in the hierarchy, never the pages the person happened to visit. The trail for a page is the same whichever way they arrived.

### Name each level literally. {#name-each-level-literally}

Use the page's own title, not a direction or a pointer.

Do: Short, literal names that match the page titles.
Don't: Names that mean nothing out of context.

## Accessibility

- **The landmark and the current page are handled.** It renders a `nav` around
  an `ol`, and the last item carries `aria-current="page"`.
- **Every breadcrumb is named "breadcrumb" unless you say otherwise.** Pass
  `label` to name the landmark. One breadcrumb per page is the shape that works;
  two with the default name produce two landmarks with the same name.
- **Keep `text` short and literal.** It is the whole accessible name of the
  link. "Autumn 2026" navigates; "here" does not.
- **The separator is generated content.** It is a `::before` on each item after
  the first, not text in the list. Browsers differ on whether they expose
  generated content to assistive technology, so do not let the character carry
  meaning — the `ol` structure is what states the nesting.
- **`id` lands on the last item.** Not on the `nav`. If you need to point a
  `aria-describedby` or a test at the trail as a whole, use `className`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `items` | arrayOf (required) | `[]` | The trail, in order, as `{ text, href, onClick }`. The last item, and any item without `href`, is the current page and is not a link. `onClick` replaces the navigation with a handler. |
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the last (current) item. |
| `separator` | node | `'/'` | What is drawn between items. A string is used as is; the default is `/`. |
| `label` | string | `'breadcrumb'` | Accessible label for the nav region that wraps the breadcrumbs. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the `nav` element beside the component's own. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the `nav` element. |

## Related

- For progress through a sequence of steps, use `ProgressTracker`. A breadcrumb is a position in a tree, not a position in a flow.
- For moving between sibling views, use `Tabs`.
- For a persistent hierarchy the user browses rather than retraces, use the Sidebar pattern.
- When the hierarchy is one level deep, a single "Back to X" link says the same thing with less furniture.
